title: Max at the Bulldog Ball
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for the McKinley Bulldogs.

pages: Every winter, McKinley families dress up for the Bulldog Ball, a big family dance in the gym at Burlingame Intermediate School. This year's theme is "A Night in Oz," and the invitation says to dress your best in pink or green, or come as your favorite character from Oz. Max spends a whole week deciding, and finally settles on the Cowardly Lion, with a fluffy yarn mane that Grandma helped sew. "A brave bulldog dressed as a scared lion," Grandma says. "That's what I call acting."

When they arrive, the parking lot smells like tacos and kettle corn. Food trucks line the curb, and a live band is warming up near the doors. Max remembers to bring a reusable water bottle, because the PTA asked everyone to cut down on waste. Inside, the gym has been transformed. A yellow paper road winds across the floor, green lights glow from the ceiling like the Emerald City, and somebody has built a giant cardboard tornado in the corner.

Max spots Lupe dressed as Glinda, in a sparkly pink dress, and Kai dressed as the Tin Man, with a funnel hat and a lot of aluminum foil. "I can't bend my elbows," Kai complains, clanking a little with every step. Then the band starts playing, and suddenly the whole gym is dancing: kindergartners, fifth graders, parents, grandparents, and even a few teachers doing a very serious version of the robot.

Max is not sure about dancing in front of so many people. For a minute, Max stands near the wall, feeling a lot like the Cowardly Lion. Then Grandma holds out her hand. "Come on," she says. "Nobody here is judging. Everybody is just having fun." Max takes a breath, steps onto the yellow paper road, and starts to dance. Two songs later, Max is leading a conga line that snakes all the way around the gym, with Kai clanking at the very end.

At dessert time, families crowd around a long table of cupcakes, cookies, and brownies donated by McKinley parents. Max chooses a green cupcake with a tiny paper ruby slipper on top. As the night winds down, the band plays one last slow song, and Max sits on the bleachers between Lupe and Kai, tired and happy. "You know what?" Max says, adjusting the floppy yarn mane. "I think the Lion found some courage tonight."

quiz.q: Why did Max say the Lion found some courage?
o: Max was nervous to dance but danced anyway
